Welcome to the titanium leg club!

I took a tumble on skis in april of 2008. took me 3 months to get back on my feet. You'll probably find yourself more aware of changes in the weather, especially pressure and temperature changes. It can be handy though, I get about a ~15 min warning before rain hits.

If you can get access to them, hot tubs have always been a godsend for me.

Glad to be part of the club!

My doctor told me the same thing. I'll know when it's going to rain or if there's going to be a difference in weather generally. I'm excited for my new meteorologist powers.

It's pretty impressive that you managed to do that on a snowboard. was the ER good, at least? mine was up in the middle of nowhere, and they didn't even have leg support on the wheelchairs. There were no beds when I arrived, so they put my leg on a folding chair. But it was broken at the knee AND the ankle, so I was turning green from pain trying to hold my knee up. I think the only thing newer than 1970, was their X-Ray machine.

They had a log of ski hill injuries though. twice as many were snowboarders, but the snowboard falls were all half as serious. a few broken arms, mostly wrist injuries. so, I'm impressed you managed that with your ankle.

Wow, I would have been so upset if my hospital was like that. Mine was actually pretty great, luckily. I was medflighted so I didn't have to wait too long to be seen. I had a bed, then my own room with a flatscreen. I honestly could not imagine having to hold my leg up for longer than 10 minutes. I was tired of it after the inital 5 minutes. That must have sucked :(

I just got lucky with my fall I think. I twisted my ankle, snapped my board, and landed on it while it was twisted. It dislocated and because of the force of me falling on the dislocation it ripped through my skin. I have never been very graceful.

Well, this IS a tiny town with a ski hill in Upper Michigan. not exactly the heart of civilization. Also, I was in too much pain to be properly upset.

It was either a Wednesday or Thursday, in a warm april, and the hill had lured my dad and I out with lodging+lift ticket deal that was only $3 more than the lift ticket woulda been. They only had the easiest lift running, so we were cutting across the top of the hill, and coming down a better run, and going fast. We'd let our momentum carry us around the base of the hill to the lift again. Except, as we crossed the bottom, I lost it, tumbled and the ski didn't come off. Fortunately for me, I was only about 20 yards from the ski patrol shack, and also fortunate was that I had leather seats, and it was easy to slide in and out of my car. Yeah, got to ride in my own car to the hospital.

Just as much fun as biting into my sweatshirt to keep from screaming, and holding up my hyper-extending broken leg, was when they were X-Raying it. Kept asking me to move it this way or that. I think I kinda snapped at them after the third time, making it clear, that no, the leg couldn't move. They were going to have to move me, or move the machine, but the leg was pretty much as-is. Funny thing, the x-ray machine DID move after I told them that.

Finally, they determined that it was broken. Gave me some drugs, which was nice so long as I was flat on my back in the ER. Not so nice once I had to start moving. This was the beginning of discovering that I have a really weird metabolism as pertains to narcotics. Whatever they gave me a shot of at the ER made it near impossible for me to crutch to the car without throwing up. Then the vicodin they gave me, the first one worked. got me through the 4 hour car ride home. The second one half worked. The third one might as well have been a tic-tac.

Wasn't until monday that I got in to see the surgeon. Was only supposed to be a 23.5 hr stay in the hospital. Turned into a 48 hour stay, because the pain was so bad. who knew that drilling titanium into bone was going to be rough, right? they gave me a pain button, but every time I hit it, I'd throw up. So... yeah. No narcotics for me, thanks.

My ankles ache in sympathy with your story. not only do I have the pin in one, but I'm with you on the whole gracefulness thing. FORTUNATELY, I'm lucky enough that none of my breaks, sprains, twists, or dislocations have broken skin.
